title: Postal address fragment sampler (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad to collect weird postal / address fragment patterns we see in user-provided contact fields, and to codify quick labeling heuristics for the micro-tasking pool. Goal is to produce a 1k-sample longtail dataset to test the address-normalizer pipeline and to create a short annotator guide for ambiguous fragments.

What this is NOT: a finished spec. It is intentionally informal — notes to self & quick decision rules so we can bootstrap labeler instructions.

Quick context:
- Problem: many product fields contain semi-structured address fragments (mix of PO box, apartment phrases, localized short forms, coordinates, or just breadcrumbs like “near the pier”). These break both parser and downstream geo/enrichment.
- Use-case: offline normalization for contact enrichment and routing (not postal validation). We prefer conservative normalization that preserves user intent.

Sampling plan (1k target):
- Pull 600 real fragments from production sampled by low-confidence region detection (p99 unmatched tokens).
- Pull 200 synthetic perturbations (typos, punctuation removal, international diacritics stripped).
- Pull 200 long-tail sources flagged by heuristic: short tokens (<6 chars) + numeric component + punctuation.
- Ensure minimum 50 examples each for: PO Box variants, intersection phrases ("& / and"), coordinate-like sequences, c/o usage, ambiguous single-word towns, apartment ranges, highway markers (I-95), ship/terminal phrases.

Labeling objectives (annotator-facing bullets):
- Primary field: "canonical_address" (free-text normalized into order: street, unit, city, region/state, postal_code, country).
- Secondary field: "ambiguity_tags" (choose 0..N from provided list: PO_BOX, C_O, INTERSECTION, COORDINATE, MAILABLE, NON_MAILABLE, LANDMARK_REF, STREET_FRAGMENT).
- Triage rule: if the fragment seems like a landmark (e.g., "behind the apple tree"), mark NON_MAILABLE + LANDMARK_REF and leave canonical_address blank.
- If unit ambiguous ("#4-6"), normalize to "Unit 4-6" (preserve hyphenation).

Heuristic cheat-sheet (for quick annotators):
- PO Box: look for tokens: box, p.o., po, pobox, p o box (case-insensitive). Normalize to "PO Box <number>". If no number, mark PO_BOX + MISSING_NUMBER.
- c/o: tokens: "c/o", "care of", "attn". Normalize to "c/o <name>" in unit position.
- Coordinates: sequences that parse as lat,long (two floats between -90..90 & -180..180) => tag COORDINATE, NON_MAILABLE.
- Intersection: patterns with "&", "@", " and ", "/" between street-like tokens ("Main & 5th") => tag INTERSECTION, canonical_address: "Main St & 5th St, <city?>" if city present.
- Highway markers: tokens like "I-95", "US Hwy 1", "Route 66" => normalize to standard highway form (I-95, US-1, Route 66).
- Postal codes: 5-digit or international formats. If postal code exists but no city, keep postal_code and leave city blank (do not infer).

Examples (raw -> normalized + tags):
1) "po box 324" -> "PO Box 324" ; ["PO_BOX","MAILABLE"]
2) "c/o john smith, 45 baker" -> "45 Baker St, c/o John Smith" ; ["C_O","MAILABLE"]
3) "near pier 7" -> "" ; ["NON_MAILABLE","LANDMARK_REF"]
4) "45b-47b king rd" -> "45B-47B King Rd" ; ["STREET_FRAGMENT","MAILABLE"]
5) "40.7128,-74.0060" -> "" ; ["COORDINATE","NON_MAILABLE"]
6) "apt 3, 140 W 4th" -> "140 W 4th St, Apt 3" ; ["MAILABLE"]
7) "pob 12" -> "PO Box 12" ; ["PO_BOX","MAILABLE"]
8) "suite 100/101, 221B Baker" -> "221B Baker St, Suite 100/101" ; ["STREET_FRAGMENT","MAILABLE"]

Ambiguities to surface (for product/engineers):
- Should we expand known abbreviations (Rd->Road, St->Street) or keep abbreviations? My leaning: preserve common short forms when they appear (consistency with OS mapping). We should have a flag to expand on export.
- Middle-eastern addressing order differences: some fragments are city-first. Annotators should avoid reordering unless confident.
- Language detection: fragments with non-latin scripts — tag NON_LATIN and punt to specialist pipeline.

Edge-case checklist (rapid scan):
- 1-letter tokens with numbers ("B 12") — often building codes or bay numbers; consider as UNIT if adjacent to street number.
- Ranges with dashes vs slashes -> preserve punctuation, but normalize whitespace.
- Mixed newline fragments (copy/paste from forms) -> collapse to single line and keep original in "raw_backup" (engineers: we will store raw).

To-dos / follow-ups:
- [ ] Create sampling SQL (DL-842) and run a smoke sample of 250 by 2026-02-15.
- [ ] Pair with geometry team to decide whether to geocode when postal_code exists but city missing. (Ping: @Miguel)
- [ ] Draft quick micro-task UI with examples (3 good / 3 bad) for labeler onboarding.
- [ ] Add exclusion list for known business shorthand that is not mailable ("Mailbox rental" etc.).

Quick regex notes (for engineer handoff):
- PO box detection: (?i) (?:p(?:\.?\s*o\.?\s*)? )?box \s*#?:?\s*([0-9]{1,6})?  -> capture number if present.
- Coordinate detection: (-?\d{1,3}\.\d+)[,;\s]+(-?\d{1,3}\.\d+)  -> then validate ranges.
- Highway:  (?:I|US|Rt|Route|Hwy)\s*-?\s*\d{1,3}  (normalize spacing).

Notes to self: keep this doc rough. When we have 200 validated samples, extract the 20 worst failure modes and iterate on rules. If labeling time > 25s per example we need to simplify the task.

Related threads / history:
- See DL-842 for sampling plan & recent run failure notes.
- Early pilot with contractors produced confusion around c/o vs attn (they used "ATTN: John" as canonical_address). Will require explicit negative examples.

Random scraps (brainstorm):
- Could mark "probable_mailingable" score (0..100) based on token-level heuristics and surface it to labelers so they can skip obvious negatives.
- Add a short video (30s) for labelers showing examples of PO Box vs building number ambiguity.

End of scratchpad.

(This file intentionally messy — copy relevant sections to confluence when we stabilize.)
